note: Automated structural checks plus manual reading of all 260 K7-K10 questions; no native-speaker or teacher review was performed, Korean-language judgements are provisional and should be confirmed by a qualified reviewer. Answer keys of all 260 questions were checked against explanations (0 mismatches); only ambiguity issues listed.

findings.question: k-k10-* (all 65)
findings.evidence: K10 questions have difficulty 1 (56) or 2 (9), mean 1.14, versus K9 mean 5.0 (65/65 at 5). Ladder is K1 1.14, K2 1.14, K3 2.14, K4 2.14, K5 3.14, K6 3.14, K7 4.14, K8 4.14, K9 5.0, K10 1.14. Root cause: scripts/learn/korean/build-korean-content.mjs uses Number(L.level[1]) so 'K10' parses as 1, giving base=1 and diagnostics 1.
findings.suggestion: Parse the level with parseInt(L.level.slice(1),10) and rebuild; decide an explicit K10 difficulty (>=5) and regenerate korean.json.

findings.question: k-k7..k10 core/variant/diagnostic
findings.evidence: Difficulty is a pure function of level (floor((n-1)/2)+1), so K7 and K8 are identical (4 for 56 items, 5 for 9), K9 is flat 5 (the +1 challenge uplift is capped away, so challenge items are no harder than core), and every one of 650 questions has expectedSeconds=30 (hard-coded). No difference between a 4-hint recognition item in K7 and one in K9; no within-level gradient across the 9 lessons.
findings.suggestion: Set difficulty per lesson/item from grammar load and string length; vary expectedSeconds by type and sentence length (K9/K10 strings average 8-9 Hangul syllables vs 3.4-4.0 in K4-K6).

findings.question: k-k6-* vs k-k7-*
findings.evidence: Mean Hangul syllables per Korean string rises from 3.6 (K6) to 7.7 (K7); distinct Korean strings drop from 75 (K6) to 42 (K7). K6 sentences are fixed survival phrases (얼마예요?, 화장실이 어디예요?, 가고 싶어요); K7 L1 immediately needs reported speech with plain-form endings (온다고, 가냐고, 오라고, 가자고) that no K1-K6 lesson teaches. The difficulty label only moves 3 -> 4.
findings.suggestion: Insert a bridge level (plain/해라체 forms, adnominals -는/-(으)ㄴ/-(으)ㄹ, basic connectors) between K6 and K7, or move indirect speech after the connector lessons.

findings.question: k-k7..k10
findings.evidence: K6 uses fill_blank (7), ordering (7), numeric (1), true_false (7), multiple_choice (43). K7, K8, K9, K10 each have only multiple_choice (56) and true_false (9); zero production (fill_blank/ordering/typing) items. Advanced grammar is therefore only tested by recognising a memorised sentence and its English gloss (same 4-8 Korean sentences per lesson reused in core, variant, diagnostic and challenge items).
findings.suggestion: Reintroduce fill_blank and ordering items (conjugate -다고/-게 하다/-(으)십시오) and at least 2 new sentences per pattern.

findings.question: k-k7-indirect_state-4, k-k7-indirect_ask-4, k-k7-indirect_cmd-4, k-k7-cause_contrast-4, k-k7-proportion-4, k-k7-appearance-4, k-k7-pretense-4, k-k7-regret-4, k-k7-review_k7-4 (and the same -4 item in K8, K9, K10)
findings.evidence: All 36 true_false items in K7-K10 have answer 'false' (K7 9/9, K8 9/9, K9 9/9, K10 9/9). K6 still has 2 'true' among 7. The pipeline (tf item: claim !== g) never emits a true claim, so 'always false' is a perfect strategy and the prompt 'Does this mean ...?' leaks the answer.
findings.suggestion: Add true claims (claim === g) for roughly half of the TF items.

findings.question: k-k7-indirect_state-1; k-k7-indirect_ask-1; k-k7-indirect_cmd-1; k-k7-indirect_cmd-2
findings.evidence: Quoted-speech lessons rely on plain-form endings -ㄴ/는다, -냐, -(으)라, -자 and on adnominal -는/-(으)ㄴ/-(으)ㄹ forms, none of which is taught in K1-K6 (K1-K6 teach only 해요체 -아/어요, -았/었어요, -(으)ㄹ 거예요, -고 싶어요, -(으)세요). Text search of K1-K10 shows 'ㄴ다고/는다고' only inside K7. Also K7 L4 오는데도, L6 오는 모양이에요, L7 아는 척해요, L8 올 걸 use adnominal forms first seen here.
findings.suggestion: Add a lesson for plain-form (해라체) verb/adjective endings and for adnominal -는/-(으)ㄴ/-(으)ㄹ before k.k7.indirect_state.

findings.question: k-k7-cause_contrast-1..4
findings.evidence: Basic connectors are not taught anywhere in K1-K10 (text search finds none of -아서/어서/해서, -지만, -(으)니까 as a connector, -(으)면 conditional, -(으)ㄹ 수 있다, -아/어야 하다, 그래서, 하지만, 그런데). K7 teaches only advanced connectors (-느라고, -는데도, -을수록, -기 마련이다) and puts them after indirect speech although the course title names conjunctions first. K10 L7 then teaches 따라서/한편/요컨대 as 'logical connectors' without 그래서/그리고/하지만.
findings.suggestion: Add core connectors (-아/어서, -(으)니까, -지만, -(으)면, -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/-아/어야 하다) before -느라고/-는데도; reorder K7 so connectors precede indirect speech.

findings.question: k-k9-biz_email-1; k-k9-biz_phone-1; k-k10-media_headline-1
findings.evidence: 합쇼체 declarative -ㅂ/습니다 is never taught: K2 has only the fixed phrases 감사합니다/반갑습니다; K8 L7 teaches only -(으)십시오/-십시다. K9 then uses it in 111 option/prompt strings (말씀드립니다, 완료했습니다, 가능하신지요, 연결해 드리겠습니다, -고자 합니다, -기 바랍니다) and K10 in 58. No lesson contrasts 해요체 and 합쇼체, and the register switch from K6/K7/K8 (해요체) to K9 is unannounced.
findings.suggestion: Add a formal-polite (-ㅂ/습니다, -ㅂ/습니까, -겠습니다) lesson in K8 before -십시오, and a register-contrast lesson at the start of K9.

findings.question: k-k8-honorific_subj-1; k-k8-honorific_subj-2; k-k8-honorific_subj-3
findings.evidence: Items use 께서 and 어머니께서 주무세요/선생님께서 편찮으세요, i.e. the subject particle 께서 and the -(으)시- suffix, but neither the particle nor the productive -(으)시- rule is taught earlier (K6 teaches -세요 only as a fixed request ending; 께서 appears nowhere before K8 L1) and the L1 concept lists only vocabulary (진지, 주무시다, 편찮으시다). Special verbs and regular -(으)시- are not contrasted.
findings.suggestion: Teach 께서/께 and -(으)시- (regular rule) before the special honorific vocabulary.

findings.lesson: Honorific L2 / Modest L8 / Formal L7
findings.question: k-k8-honorific_obj-1; k-k8-modesty-2; k-k8-formal_style-1
findings.evidence: Humble forms are split: 드리다/뵙다/여쭙다 are in L2 (called 'object honorific') while 저희 and 말씀 올리다 are in L8 after the formal-style lesson. -십시오 (L7) is taught before the declarative formal ending it belongs with. Subject and object honorifics are in adjacent lessons, but humble (겸양) vocabulary is separated by four voice lessons.
findings.suggestion: Order: -(으)시- / 께서, special vocabulary, humble verbs and 저희 (merge L2 and L8), then formal styles.

findings.question: k-k8-passive_compound-2; k-k8-passive_compound-3; k-k8-causative_compound-1
findings.evidence: The voice block is passive affix (L3), -어지다/-게 되다 (L4), causative affix (L5), -게 하다 (L6). The affix passive and affix causative share -이/히/리/기- and are separated by a lesson that is not a passive in the strict sense (-게 되다 means 'come to be / end up', and 글씨가 써져요 is a 'writes well' middle use), and -게 되다 comes before -게 하다 although the pair is usually contrasted. A learner meets 열려요 (passive) and 먹여요 (causative) two lessons apart with no contrast item.
findings.suggestion: Pair passive/causative affixes (e.g. 보다-보이다-보여 주다), then -어지다/-게 되다 vs -게 하다; label -게 되다 as 'become/come to'.

findings.question: k-k8-passive_affix-1; k-k8-passive_affix-2; k-k8-passive_affix-3
findings.evidence: Concept names -이/히/리/기- passives but all items are inchoative/intransitive-like (문이 열려요, 창문이 닫혀요, 산이 보여요, 음악이 들려요); no agentive passive with 에게/에 의해 (e.g. 경찰에게 잡혔어요) and no -기- example. Causative lesson L5 names -우- but gives only 보여 주다, 먹여요, 입혀요 (no 자다-재우다, 타다-태우다).
findings.suggestion: Add one example per suffix, including an agentive passive and a -우- causative.

findings.question: k-k7-d2; k-k8-d1; k-k8-d2; k-k9-d2; k-k10-d2
findings.evidence: Diagnostic items are attached to the first two skills of each level but test later lessons: k-k7-d2 (skill indirect_ask) tests 비가 오는데도 갔어요 (L4); k-k8-d1 (honorific_subj) tests 선물을 드려요 (L2); k-k8-d2 (honorific_obj) tests 자리에 앉으십시오 (L7); k-k9-d2 (biz_phone) tests 상호 협력을 희망합니다 (L7); k-k10-d2 (media_article) tests 일석이조예요 (L6). A diagnostic on skill X therefore measures unrelated, later grammar and distorts mastery/prerequisite estimates.
findings.suggestion: Generate diagnostics from items of the same skill (or tag them with the skill they test).

findings.question: k-k10-media_headline-1; k-k10-media_headline-3; k-k10-media_headline-2
findings.evidence: Concept says 'compressed noun phrases: 물가 안정 대책 발표' but every item is a full sentence ending in -했습니다/-하고 있습니다, so no headline (noun-final/ellipsed) style is taught or tested. 인공지능 기술이 발전하고 있습니다 also needs the progressive -고 있다 which no earlier lesson teaches (it first appears in K10).
findings.suggestion: Use real headline forms (물가 안정 대책 발표, 수출 사상 최대) and teach -고 있다 earlier.

findings.question: k-k10-logic_debate-1; k-k10-media_article-1
findings.evidence: Discourse markers 한편/따라서/요컨대/-에 따르면 are taught in L7, after the editorial reading lesson (L2) that already depends on connected prose, and after four lessons of idioms/proverbs/사자성어. K10 devotes 4 of 9 lessons (L3-L6) to figurative language while reading/argument skills get 2.
findings.suggestion: Move discourse markers before the editorial lesson; reduce idiom share or place idioms after the argument lessons.

findings.question: k-k9-biz_etiquette-1; k-k9-biz_etiquette-2
findings.evidence: Introductions and titles (처음 뵙겠습니다, 명함, 부장님/팀장님) are the first step of a business interaction and are needed to address emails and phone calls in L1-L2, yet are taught 8th. Rank vocabulary is also incomplete (사원-대리-과장-차장-부장 ladder absent; 팀장 is a role, not a rank).
findings.suggestion: Move to L1 and add the title ladder.

findings.question: k-k7-indirect_state-1 ('friend said coming'), k-k7-indirect_state-2 ('weather said good'), k-k7-appearance-2 ('seems raining'), k-k10-idioms_body-2 ('high standards choose'), k-k9-biz_etiquette-1 ('pleased to meet card'), k-k8-honorific_obj-1 ('give gift honorific'), k-k10-review_k10-1 ('achieved two birds effect'), k-k8-passive_affix-3 ('mountain seen')
findings.evidence: English glosses are telegraphic strings derived from camelCase keys (friendSaidComing, weatherSaidGood, giveGiftHonorific, highStandardsChoose) rather than sentences, and are shown as answer options and in explanations. Many are ungrammatical or misleading: 'seems raining', 'high standards choose' (눈이 높아요 = has high standards / is picky), 'pleased to meet card' for 처음 뵙겠습니다, 명함 드립니다 (= Nice to meet you; here is my card), 'letter written well' for 글씨가 써져요 (글씨 = handwriting), 'dresses clothes' for 동생에게 옷을 입혀요 (dresses the younger sibling), 'give gift honorific' (드리다 is a humble verb). Subjects/tense are lost: 친구가 온다고 해요 is present ('says') but glossed 'said'.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite glosses as natural English sentences (e.g. 'A friend says (they) are coming.') and review them; keep native-language review as a separate step.

findings.question: k-k7-indirect_state-1 vs k-k7-review_k7-v2 and k-k7-review_k7-1
findings.evidence: 친구가 온다고 해요 (present, k-k7-indirect_state-1) and 친구가 온다고 했어요 (past, k-k7-review_k7-1) both carry the gloss 'friend said coming'; k-k7-review_k7-v2 'Choose the Korean for “friend said coming”' offers only the 했어요 form, while k-k7-indirect_state-3 uses the 해요 form for 'rain said coming'. The tense distinction is lost, so the same English maps to two Korean forms across the course.
findings.suggestion: Gloss 해요 as 'says' and 했어요 as 'said'.

findings.question: k-k7-indirect_state-c, k-k8-honorific_subj-c, k-k9-biz_email-c, k-k10-media_headline-c (36 total in K7-K10, 7 in K6)
findings.evidence: Every listening challenge question has the explanation: “…” (romanization) means “”. The gloss slot is empty because the listen item has no g, so the explanation ends in an empty quotation (`means “”`). Present in all 36 K7-K10 -c items and 7 K6 items.
findings.suggestion: Fill the gloss for listen items (use the gloss of the correct option) in build-korean-content.mjs.

findings.question: k-k8-honorific_obj-3, k-k8-honorific_obj-v1, k-k9-biz_report-2, k-k9-biz_report (lesson example)
findings.evidence: Romanization errors: '여쭤봐요' is romanized 'yeojjjwobwayo' (three j) in k-k8-honorific_obj-3/-v1 hints and explanations; 조치를 완료했습니다 is romanized 'jochireul wallyeohaesseoyo' in k-k9-biz_report-2 and the L5 lesson example, which both mismatches the -습니다 ending (haesseumnida) and misspells 완료 (wallyo). K10 shows 'chinhwan-gyeong' with a stray hyphen. Hints read these aloud to the learner.
findings.suggestion: Fix romanization strings (yeojjwobwayo; jochireul wallyohaesseumnida; chinhwangyeong).

findings.question: k-k10-idioms_action-3, k-k10-idioms_action-v1, k-k10-idioms_action-c, k-k10-idioms_action-v2
findings.evidence: The taught idiom is written 발을 벗고 나섰어요 ('stepped up to help'). The usual set phrase is 발 벗고 나서다 (no 을); with 을 it reads literally as taking off a foot/shoes, and the distractor in k-k10-idioms_action-v1 is 'took off shoes', so the keyed answer is a non-standard form of the idiom and is confusable with the literal reading.
findings.suggestion: Change to 발 벗고 나섰어요 and replace the 'took off shoes' distractor or add context.

findings.question: k-k9-biz_stats-v2
findings.evidence: Prompt 'Choose the Korean for “sales increased”' has two valid options: a 매출이 증가했습니다 (keyed) and d 매출이 올랐습니다 (rose/increased). Both express sales increased; only one is credited.
findings.suggestion: Remove 매출이 올랐습니다 or change the prompt to specify the register ('rose' vs formal 'increased').

findings.question: k-k9-biz_phone-3, k-k9-biz_phone-v1, k-k9-review_k9-3
findings.evidence: 메모를 남겨 드릴까요? is glossed 'shall i take message' (lowercase 'i'). 남겨 드리다 means to leave something for someone ('Shall I leave a note/message for you?'); 'take a message' would be a different expression. The same phrase appears as 메모를 남겨 드립니다 in k-k9-review_k9-3 distractor.
findings.suggestion: Gloss as 'Shall I leave a message for you?' or change the phrase to a natural 'take a message' expression, and capitalise.

findings.question: k-k8-formal_style-2, k-k8-formal_style-c, k-k8-formal_style-v1
findings.evidence: 출발하십시다 ('let us depart') is taught as the propositive pair of -하십시오. The standard 하십시오체 propositive is -(ㅂ/으)ㅂ시다 (출발합시다); -(으)십시다 is rarely used and sounds dated. Presenting it as the model form may mislead learners (flag for qualified Korean-language review).
findings.suggestion: Use 출발합시다 or drop the propositive; explain that -(으)십시오 is the imperative.

findings.question: k-k10-logic_debate-1, k-k10-logic_debate-3, k-k10-logic_debate-v1
findings.evidence: Sentences are artificial: 의견에 따르면 그렇습니다 (-에 따르면 expects a source such as 보도/연구, not 'opinion'); 따라서 결론입니다 ('therefore conclusion') is unnatural (따라서 결론은 ...), 반면에 그렇습니다 is an incomplete contrast. They are isolated fragments, not discourse.
findings.suggestion: Replace with natural example sentences (e.g. 연구에 따르면 ...; 따라서 ...를 제안합니다).

findings.question: k-k8-passive_compound-1, k-k8-passive_compound-3, k-k8-passive_compound-v1
findings.evidence: 한국에 가게 되었어요 is glossed 'went to korea result' (it means 'I ended up going / it turned out that I go to Korea'; 'went' loses the -게 되다 nuance); 글씨가 써져요 'letter written well' mixes 글씨 (handwriting) with 'letter' (mail/character) and is an uncommon textbook example of -어지다.
findings.suggestion: Gloss as 'I ended up going to Korea'; consider a more common -어지다 example (e.g. 길이 만들어졌어요) after qualified review.

findings.question: k-k10-media_article-1, k-k10-media_headline-3, k-k10-culture_deep-3, k-k10-culture_deep-2
findings.evidence: Glosses do not match the Korean: 친환경 에너지가 주목받고 있습니다 ('clean energy popular' - 주목받다 = attracts attention); 인공지능 기술이 발전하고 있습니다 ('ai developing rapidly' - 'rapidly' is not in the Korean); 음식을 나눠 먹어요 ('share food neighbors' - no neighbors in the sentence); 송편을 빚어요 ('make songpyeon chuseok' - Chuseok not in the sentence). 'ai' lower-case.
findings.suggestion: Gloss literally and keep cultural context in the lesson concept, not the answer.

findings.lesson: Deep Korean cultural values and customs
findings.question: k-k10-culture_deep-v2; k-k10-sino_four-v2
findings.evidence: k-k10-culture_deep-v2 'warm jeong affection': distractor d 정이 많아요 ('has a lot of jeong') is nearly equivalent to the keyed 따뜻한 정이 있어요. k-k10-sino_four-v2 'two birds one stone': distractor c 두 마리 토끼. is the Korean idiom equivalent (두 마리 토끼를 잡다), so it is arguably also correct.
findings.suggestion: Replace the near-synonym distractors.

findings.question: k-k8-honorific_obj-1, k-k8-d1, k-k8-honorific_obj-2
findings.evidence: 선물을 드려요 is glossed 'give gift honorific' with no recipient; 드리다 is a humble verb and needs a recipient (할머니께 선물을 드려요 as in k-k8-review_k8-1). 'honorific' is added to glosses of 봬요/여쭤봐요 instead of 'to an elder'. 내일 봬요 teaches the 봬요 form of 뵙다 without showing 뵙다 itself, although the concept lists 뵙다.
findings.suggestion: Add the recipient (할머니께) and gloss 'give (to an elder)'.

findings.question: k-k10-idioms_body-1, k-k10-idioms_body-2, k-k10-idioms_action-1, k-k10-proverbs_life-2
findings.evidence: Distractors pre-show later lessons: L3 options contain 'ripped off price' and 'heavy responsibility burden' (L4), proverb L5 options contain 'three days resolve' and 'two birds one stone' (L6), K9 L1 options contain 'connecting person in charge' (L2). Title says 발, 눈, 귀, 손 but 손 is never taught (손이 커요 appears only as a distractor).
findings.suggestion: Draw distractors from the current or earlier lessons; add 손이 크다 or remove 손 from the title.

findings.question: k-k9-biz_etiquette-2, k-k9-biz_etiquette-1
findings.evidence: 김 부장님입니다 is glossed 'department manager kim' while the distractor is 'general manager lee'; 부장 is rendered both ways in English, so the gloss pair is ambiguous in principle. 처음 뵙겠습니다, 명함 드립니다 is an uncommon pairing (명함 드리겠습니다 / 제 명함입니다 is more usual).
findings.suggestion: Use a consistent title translation and a more natural card phrase.

findings.question: k-k9-biz_schedule-2, k-k9-biz_schedule-1
findings.evidence: 너른 양해 부탁드립니다 is used in business writing but 넓은/너그러운 양해 부탁드립니다 or 양해 부탁드립니다 are more usual; 너른 is the rarer form. Also the L3 concept introduces -고자 합니다 without explanation.
findings.suggestion: Confirm with qualified reviewer; consider 양해 부탁드립니다.

findings.question: (doc not found)
findings.evidence: The file named in the task, docs/learning/korean-standard-2020-coverage.md, does not exist in this checkout (docs/learning only contains curriculum-2022-coverage.md, which maps math, and language-urls-and-korean-host.md). No repo document maps K1-K10 to a Korean-language standard, so alignment below is judged against the generally described six-level KSL framework (levels 1-2 beginner, 3-4 intermediate, 5-6 advanced) and needs human confirmation.
findings.suggestion: Add the coverage doc (level-by-level mapping with can-do statements) to the repo.

findings.question: k.k7..k.k10 skills
findings.evidence: K1-K6 cover beginner survival content (levels 1-2 equivalent). K7-K10 jump directly to advanced grammar and registers: K7 reported speech and advanced connectors (usually levels 4-5), K8 honorific/voice/formal (3-5), K9 workplace in 합쇼체 (5-6), K10 idioms/proverbs/사자성어 (5-6). Intermediate (level 3-4) staples are missing: -아/어서, -(으)니까, -지만, -(으)면, -(으)ㄹ 수 있다, -아/어야 하다, -고 있다, -(으)ㄹ까요, comparatives (보다, 더/가장), adnominal forms, -는 것, -기 때문에, -(으)려고, -도록, plus topics such as health, housing, education, travel, social issues. No lesson requires producing a paragraph; all items are single sentences with recognition tasks, so reading/writing/discourse outcomes of the upper levels are not covered.
findings.suggestion: Insert an intermediate bridge track (K6.5/K7) and add paragraph-level reading/listening/production items to K9-K10.

findings.question: k-k9-biz_email-1, k-k9-biz_meeting-1, k-k9-biz_stats-1
findings.evidence: K9 assumes a workplace learner and a single register (합쇼체 with 드립니다/주십시오/바랍니다/하고자 합니다/가능하신지요). Vocabulary (안건, 매출, 절충안, 체결, 담당자, 전년 대비) is specialised and never pre-taught (no business vocabulary in K1-K8), while general social/academic topics at the same level are absent. Emails and meeting phrases are given as one-line fragments rather than complete email/meeting text.
findings.suggestion: State the target audience, pre-teach vocabulary in K8, and add 해요체 workplace conversation (colleagues) alongside 합쇼체.

findings.question: bk-ko-k7..k10 (351 each)
findings.evidence: Each of K7-K10 has 351 bank questions but only 3 distinct prompts (117 copies of each, options shuffled), the same for K1-K10; difficulty is 2/3/4 in exactly 117 each at every level (mean 3.0 for K1-K10, no progression), expectedSeconds 40, all multiple_choice. skillIds do not match content: bk-ko-k7-k-k7-indirect_ask-039 asks about -(으)ㄹ 걸 그랬어요; bk-ko-k7-k-k7-proportion-010 asks about -다고 하다; bk-ko-k8-k-k8-passive_affix-039 asks about 드리다; bk-ko-k8-k-k8-causative_affix-034 asks about -(으)시-; bk-ko-k10-k-k10-sino_four-025 asks about 발이 넓다; bk-ko-k10-k-k10-media_headline-017 asks about the proverb 가는 말이 고와야...; bk-ko-k9-k-k9-biz_negotiate-004 asks about email attachments.
findings.suggestion: Regenerate the bank per skill with distinct items and level-specific difficulty; re-tag skillIds.
